newsitem.title: CHINA: China economy in best shape of 1990s - think tank.
newsitem.headline: China economy in best shape of 1990s - think tank.

text.p: China's economy is in the best shape so far in the 1990s but Beijing should maintain relatively tight control over the economy to ensure stable growth, a report by a Chinese government think tank said on Friday.

The Chinese economy was seen growing by about 10 percent in 1997, up slightly from last year's 9.7 percent, said the report by a group of economists from the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the State Statistics Bureau.
Retail price inflation, China's benchmark figure, was seen at five percent this year while consumer prices were seen rising by seven percent, the Xinhua news agency quoted the report as saying.
Beijing's austerity campaign succeeded in controlling retail price inflation at 6.1 percent in 1996, down from 14.8 percent the year before.
Growth in fixed assets investment in 1997 would match last year's level of 12.7 percent, the report said.
Urban incomes would grow by 4.9 percent and rural incomes were seen rising by 5.3 percent in 1997, it said.
However, there were still many problems in the economy, Xinhua quoted the report as saying but gave no further details.
